summary: Radar for 2026-10-28, GLP-1 focus. I checked the leading candidates on the web. No signal today meets the Lane C bar (a randomized efficacy result on a named next-gen drug, first public within 48 hours). UBT251's Phase 2 numbers in Cell Metabolism first came out in March 2026. The tradipitant Phase 3 result (Vanda Study 3601) is for an anti-nausea add-on, not a GLP-1, and S2 10-28 already covered it as a Short. Two near-term events could change that. Lilly reports Q3 results on Oct 29, and Novo expects the FDA decision on CagriSema in Q4 (only the quarter is public). Treat both as watchlist items: only a randomized result first published within 48 hours goes to Lane C. Approvals and status-only news become Shorts. The best long-form picks are the Lane A practical tirzepatide queue, each with a fresh hook: protein and muscle; stopping, refreshed by CBC (Oct 27) and the Metabolites regain review; nausea, refreshed by tradipitant; exercise and running, refreshed by the Guardian (Oct 27); hair loss; and plateaus. Strong Short and Instagram picks: ACOG's new pregnancy guidance (caution), the gallbladder and pancreas cohort, Halloween and Thanksgiving, and retatrutide sleep apnea only with a 'what's confirmed?' angle (it's peaking). Rejected: the PR naming the 'cheapest' place to buy compounded tirzepatide online, retatrutide 'research vial' pricing, and anything about microdosing.

candidates.topic: Protein on tirzepatide: how much, and why it protects muscle. New J Clin Med study (Oct 15, 2026) on weight-loss size, fat mass and device-estimated muscle loss during obesity medication
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form, next in the playbook queue. Open with a 'you' scenario: 'You're eating half what you used to. Here's why protein matters more now.' Give general guidance from nutrition societies and obesity-medicine advisories, with no prescription-drug dosing. Link it to the Bones and Muscle and Strength Training videos so YouTube suggests them together. Cite the SURMOUNT-1 body-scan split to Look et al. 2025.
candidates.why_now: Muscle loss has been in our radar for 8 snapshots in a row and is still rising (72). There's a new real-world study of muscle loss, plus press on 'muscle-saving' add-ons (Longevity.Technology NAD+ piece, Oct 27) that people will ask about. Lane A videos earn about 2.4× the channel median in watch minutes.

evidence.signal: Weight-loss size, fat mass and device-estimated muscle loss during obesity medication
'Can an NAD+ booster protect muscle on semaglutide?': public curiosity about protecting muscle

candidates.topic: What happens when you stop tirzepatide? SURMOUNT-4 regain, a new systematic review of regain after GLP-1 and GIP/GLP-1 medicines (Metabolites, Oct 9), and CBC's 'Everyone's going on and off GLP-1s' (Oct 27)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form, third in the queue. The first sentence answers the title: most people regain part of the weight they lost when they stop. Use exact SURMOUNT-4 numbers: 335 versus 335 randomized at week 36, and the +14.0% regain counted from week 36 to week 88. Then cover what the evidence says helps keep results, and say clearly: 'don't stop or change your medicine on your own; talk to your prescriber.'
keywords: what happens when you stop tirzepatide
candidates.predicted_peak: steady, with a spike in early January
candidates.why_now: CBC's mainstream piece on going 'on and off' GLP-1s (Oct 27), a new regain review, and 7 combined appearances across our past snapshots. Coverage cuts to employer plans for 2027 (CNBC, Oct 27) will push more people to search what happens if they stop.

evidence.signal: Systematic review of weight regain after stopping GLP-1 and GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonists
'Everyone's going on — and off — GLP-1s. What's that doing to your health?'

candidates.topic: Nausea and vomiting on tirzepatide: what actually helps, refreshed by the tradipitant (NEREUS) Phase 3 result. Vomiting in 43.0% (61/142) versus 58.5% (96/164) after a single untitrated 1 mg semaglutide dose (Vanda Study 3601, HCPLive Oct 27)
candidates.angle: A Lane A long-form, 'Tirzepatide Nausea: What Helps?', using everyday habits from the trials and guidance (smaller meals, eating slower, stopping at fullness, fluids, less greasy food) plus when to call your prescriber. Mention tradipitant only as investigational for this use: a company topline result, not yet peer-reviewed, given with one untitrated semaglutide dose rather than tirzepatide. The 08:00 Short is already done (S2 10-28), so don't repeat the trial in a Short this week.
keywords: how to stop nausea on tirzepatide
candidates.predicted_peak: 3–10 days for the news; the core query is evergreen
candidates.why_now: Vanda's Phase 3 announcement (Oct 27) was picked up by Fierce Pharma, HCPLive and Dealroom, and Vanda plans to file a supplemental NDA. Nausea was our second-best body-worry Short (149 views) and an Instagram winner (120).

evidence.signal: Phase 3: 43.0% versus 58.5% vomiting; frequent vomiting 6.3% versus 15.9%
Study 3601 results; single 1 mg semaglutide dose without titration

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide hair loss: how common is it and what helps? Systematic review of skin side effects (Med Sci Basel, Oct 9) and the July 2026 matched cohort (tirzepatide RR 1.68, semaglutide RR 1.43)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form, fourth in the queue. The first sentence answers 'how common': give the trial rates with the placebo rate next to them, then explain that rapid weight loss itself is linked to temporary shedding (telogen effluvium). Cover what helps: enough protein, avoiding crash eating, and seeing a doctor if shedding persists. Describe the cohort as observational, 'linked to'.
keywords: hair loss on weight loss injection
candidates.why_now: It's in the playbook queue, refreshed by new reviews, and searched heavily by tirzepatide users. Many hair-loss videos are anecdotal, so an evidence-led one stands out.

evidence.signal: Systematic review of cutaneous adverse events with semaglutide, liraglutide and tirzepatide

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide weight-loss plateau: what the trials and new real-world data show. Post-initiation care and weight loss in clinical practice (medRxiv, Oct 6) and a real-world semaglutide/tirzepatide cohort from Türkiye (J Clin Med, Oct 13)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form, fifth in the queue. Open: 'Your weight stopped moving at month 9. That's the curve the trials show too.' Explain why the SURMOUNT-1 curves flatten (the body adapts) and what the real-world data link to better results, such as follow-up visits and dietitian support. No titration advice: 'ask your prescriber'.
keywords: why did my weight loss stop on tirzepatide
candidates.why_now: Two fresh real-world papers on what follow-up care links to. People search 'stopped working' heavily, and the topic fits the Life on Tirzepatide playlist.

evidence.signal: Post-initiation care patterns and weight loss with semaglutide and tirzepatide in clinical practice
